items.label: Lemma 1
items.statementHtml: Let $j\ge0$. Suppose that the polar data have $\rho_k,\zeta_k>0$ and $Z_k\succ0$ for $k=2j,2j+1,2j+2$, and that $0<\delta_k<\pi$ and $(Z_k)_{12}>0$ for $k=2j,2j+1$. The following statements hold for $k=2j,2j+1$: \textup{i)} a unique $\alpha_k>0$ satisfying $s_k=-\alpha_kH_kg_k$ exists if and only if $r_k=\cos\delta_k+h_k\sin\delta_k$; \textup{ii)} if the relations in part~\textup{i)} hold and $p_k^Tq_k>0$ at both stages, then [eq:dfp-update] is equivalent to Z_{k+1}=R(\delta_k)^T \left[ \left(I-\frac{q_kp_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k}\right)Z_k \left(I-\frac{p_kq_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k}\right) +\frac{q_kq_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k} \right]R(\delta_k).

items.label: Lemma 2
items.statementHtml: Let $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$. Suppose $0<\delta_k<\pi$, $h_k>0$, $\rho_k,\rho_{k+1},\zeta_k,\zeta_{k+1}>0$, and $r_k=\rho_k/\rho_{k+1}=\cos\delta_k+h_k\sin\delta_k$. Then $g_k^Ts_k<0$, and the prescribed values and gradients satisfy the strong Wolfe conditions if and only if(分别编号) \frac{\rho_k^2-\rho_{k+1}^2}{-2g_k^Ts_k} &=\frac{r_k^2-1}{2\zeta_kh_k\sin\delta_k\,r_k}\ge\eta_1,\\ \frac{|g_{k+1}^Ts_k|}{|g_k^Ts_k|} &=\frac{\zeta_{k+1}}{\zeta_k} \frac{|h_k\cos\delta_k-\sin\delta_k|}{h_kr_k}\le\eta_2.

items.label: Proposition 3
items.statementLatex:
\label{prop:polar-realization}
Suppose that
\textup{i)} for every $k\ge0$, the polar data satisfy
$\rho_k,\zeta_k>0$, $Z_k\succ0$, $(Z_k)_{12}>0$,
$0<\delta_k<\pi$, $p_k^Tq_k>0$, and
$r_k=\cos\delta_k+h_k\sin\delta_k$;
\textup{ii)} for fixed $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$,
\eqref{eq:polar-matrix-map} and \eqref{eq:polar-wolfe-ratios}
hold for every $k\ge0$;
\textup{iii)} a single function $f\in C^1(\mathbb R^2)$ satisfies
$f(x_k)=F_k$ and $\nabla f(x_k)=g_k$ for all $k\ge0$.
Then there are positive step lengths for which classical DFP initialized at
$x_0,H_0$ generates exactly the prescribed points and matrices and
satisfies the strong Wolfe conditions at every step.

Then there are positive step lengths for which classical DFP initialized at $x_0,H_0$ generates exactly the prescribed points and matrices and satisfies the strong Wolfe conditions at every step.

items.label: Lemma 4
items.statementHtml: Fix $X\succ0$ with $\xi>0$, and for each $\tau>0$ set $Z_k=S_\tau^{-1}XS_\tau^{-1}$. If $\delta_k/\tau\to\bar\delta>0$ and $\zeta_k,\zeta_{k+1}\to1$ as $\tau\downarrow0$, then the update [eq:polar-matrix-map] is well defined for all sufficiently small $\tau>0$, and $S_\tau Z_{k+1}S_\tau$ tends to the symmetric matrix X_+=\gamma_+&\xi_+\\\xi_+&\eta_+ =\gamma&\gamma(\bar h-\bar\delta)\\\gamma(\bar h-\bar\delta)&1+\gamma(\bar h-\bar\delta)^2.

items.label: Lemma 5
items.statementLatex:
\label{lem:polar-parameter-choice}
For every $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, one can choose positive angular
coefficients and a base point $\nu_*$ in the positivity interval of
\eqref{eq:polar-family} so that, with $\gamma_*=\gamma(\nu_*)$,
the following hold: \textup{i)} at both the even and odd stages,
the limiting Armijo and strong-curvature ratios are respectively
above $\eta_1$ and below $\eta_2$;
\textup{ii)} at the even state corresponding to $\nu_*$, with
$\gamma=\gamma_*$ fixed, the derivative of the complete limiting
cycle in $(\xi,\eta)$ has spectral radius less than one;
\textup{iii)} $\gamma'(\nu_*)>0$, so $\gamma(\nu)$ has an analytic
local inverse $\nu(\gamma)$ near $\gamma_*$.
items.statementHtml: For every $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, one can choose positive angular coefficients and a base point $ u_*$ in the positivity interval of [eq:polar-family] so that, with $\gamma_*=\gamma( u_*)$, the following hold: extup{i)} at both the even and odd stages, the limiting Armijo and strong-curvature ratios are respectively above $\eta_1$ and below $\eta_2$; extup{ii)} at the even state corresponding to $ u_*$, with $\gamma=\gamma_*$ fixed, the derivative of the complete limiting cycle in $(\xi,\eta)$ has spectral radius less than one; extup{iii)} $\gamma'( u_*)>0$, so $\gamma( u)$ has an analytic local inverse $ u(\gamma)$ near $\gamma_*$.

items.label: Lemma 6
items.statementLatex:
\label{lem:polar-cycle-estimates}
Fix a positive analytic function $\phi$ on a neighborhood of the
chosen $\gamma$ interval, and let $\Phi$ be the complete cycle defined
above. Then $\Phi$ extends analytically to $\tau^2=v=0$.
After shrinking the chosen $\gamma$ interval about $\gamma_*$ if
necessary, there are a fixed norm
$|\cdot|_*$, $0<q<1$, and $\kappa_0>0$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:polar-fast-bound}
\begin{aligned}
 |u_+|_*&\le q|u|_*+\kappa_0(v+\tau^2)+\kappa_0|u|_*^2,\\
 \gamma_+&=\gamma+v\psi_\phi(\gamma)
          +O(v|u|_*+v^2+\tau^2),
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}\label{eq:polar-slow-drift}
 \psi_\phi(\gamma)
 =2\gamma\nu(\gamma)
 \left(\bar\delta_{\mathrm E}^{-1}+\bar\delta_{\mathrm O}^{-1}\right)
 \phi(\gamma)-\frac{2\gamma}{1+\beta}.
\end{equation}
The bounds are uniform for sufficiently small $\tau^2,v\ge0$ and states
in a fixed neighborhood of the even reference curve, with constants
depending on $\phi$.

The bounds are uniform for sufficiently small $\tau^2,v\ge0$ and states in a fixed neighborhood of the even reference curve, with constants depending on $\phi$.

items.label: Lemma 7
items.statementLatex:
\label{lem:polar-continuation}
For every sufficiently large $j_0$, the recurrence
\eqref{eq:polar-matrix-map}, initialized by
\eqref{eq:polar-initial-matrix}, with the angles in
\eqref{eq:polar-angles} and the gradient factors in
\eqref{eq:polar-feedback}, defines an infinite matrix sequence. For all $j\ge0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:polar-tube-estimates}
 \gamma_j=\gamma_*+O(\tau_j^{1-\beta}),\qquad
 X_j-X_{\mathrm E}(\gamma_j)=O(\tau_j^{1+\beta}).
\end{equation}
The odd normalized matrices satisfy
$S_{\tau_j}Z_{2j+1}S_{\tau_j}=X_{\mathrm O}(\gamma_j)+O(\tau_j^{1+\beta})$.
Every matrix $Z_k$ is positive definite, and
$(Z_k)_{12}>0$, $r_k>0$, and $p_k^Tq_k>0$.
The constants are independent of $j_0$ once $j_0$ exceeds a fixed threshold.

For all $j\ge0$, \gamma_j=\gamma_*+O(\tau_j^{1-\beta}),\qquad X_j-X_{\mathrm E}(\gamma_j)=O(\tau_j^{1+\beta}). The odd normalized matrices satisfy $S_{\tau_j}Z_{2j+1}S_{\tau_j}=X_{\mathrm O}(\gamma_j)+O(\tau_j^{1+\beta})$. Every matrix $Z_k$ is positive definite, and $(Z_k)_{12}>0$, $r_k>0$, and $p_k^Tq_k>0$. The constants are independent of $j_0$ once $j_0$ exceeds a fixed threshold.

items.label: Lemma 8
items.statementHtml: For sufficiently large $j_0$, the points in [eq:polar-radii] have accumulation set $\Gamma=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\|x\|=1\}$ and satisfy \|x_m-x_k\|\ge \kappa_-\max\{\tau_{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}, \tau_{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}\} \qquad(m\ne k), where $\kappa_->0$ is independent of $j_0$. Moreover, $\|s_k\|\asymp\tau_{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}$, $\|g_k-x_k\|=O(\tau_{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}^{1+\beta})$, and the endpoint data $F_k,g_k$ satisfy the strong Wolfe inequalities at every step. The comparison constants are independent of $j_0$.

items.label: Lemma 9
items.statementHtml: Let $x_k,g_k,F_k$ be the data in Lemma~[lem:polar-geometry], with $j_0$ sufficiently large. Then there is a function $f\in C^2(\mathbb R^2)$ whose Hessian is globally $ eta$-H\"older continuous and which agrees with $\|x\|^2/2$ on the closed unit disk. At every prescribed point, f(x_k)=F_k= rac{1}{2} ho_k^2,\qquad abla f(x_k)=g_k,\qquad abla^2f(x_k)=I. Writing $\Psi=f-\|x\|^2/2$, there is a constant $\kappa$ independent of the final choice of $j_0$ such that \sup_{x\in\mathbb R^2}\| abla^2\Psi(x)\|\le \kappa au_0^ eta.

items.label: Theorem 10
items.statementLatex:
\label{thm:main}
For every integer $n\ge2$, $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$,
$\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, and $\beta\in(0,1)$, there exist
$f\in C^2(\R^n)$, $x_0\in\R^n$, a positive definite matrix
$H_0\in\R^{n\times n}$, and a sequence of positive step lengths
such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]
$(1-\varepsilon)I\preceq\nabla^2f(x)\preceq(1+\varepsilon)I$
for all $x\in\R^n$, and the origin is the unique minimizer.
\item[(ii)]
The Hessian is globally $\beta$-H\"older continuous and has no
H\"older bound of any exponent $\beta'\in(\beta,1]$ on the
initial level set $\{x:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}$.
\item[(iii)]
The resulting infinite classical DFP sequence satisfies the
standard strong Wolfe conditions with parameters $(\eta_1,\eta_2)$
at every iteration, but $\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to1$.
Its accumulation set is the unit circle centered at the origin
in a two-dimensional subspace of $\R^n$.
\end{enumerate}

Its accumulation set is the unit circle centered at the origin in a two-dimensional subspace of $\R^n$.

items.label: Corollary 11
items.statementLatex:
\label{cor:identity-initialization}
For every integer $n\ge2$, $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$,
and $\beta\in(0,1)$, a strongly convex objective function
$\widetilde f\in C^2(\R^n)$ with globally $\beta$-H\"older continuous
Hessian admits an infinite classical DFP sequence initialized with
$\widetilde H_0=I$, satisfying the standard strong Wolfe conditions
with parameters $(\eta_1,\eta_2)$ and
$\liminf_k\|\nabla\widetilde f(\widetilde x_k)\|>0$.
The origin is its unique minimizer, $\widetilde f(0)=0$, and its Hessian
has positive global lower and upper bounds that may depend on the
example. The accumulation set is an ellipse centered at the origin
in a two-dimensional subspace.

The origin is its unique minimizer, $\widetilde f(0)=0$, and its Hessian has positive global lower and upper bounds that may depend on the example. The accumulation set is an ellipse centered at the origin in a two-dimensional subspace.

items.label: Lemma 12
items.statementLatex:
\label{lem:planar-degeneration}
Let $f\in C^2(\R^2)$ be $m$-strongly convex, where $m>0$.
Consider an infinite sequence of nonstationary iterates with
$g_k=\nabla f(x_k)$, $s_k=-\alpha_kH_kg_k$,
$x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k$, and $y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k$, where $H_k\succ0$,
$\alpha_k>0$, and every step satisfies \eqref{eq:armijo} and
\eqref{eq:weak-curvature} for fixed $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$.
Suppose $H_ky_{k-1}=s_{k-1}$ for $k\ge1$. Put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:planar-scalar-definition}
\kappa_k=\frac{s_k^Ty_k}{\|s_k\|^2}\quad(k\ge0),\qquad
\lambda_k=\kappa_{k-1}\det H_k\quad(k\ge1).
\end{equation}
If $x_k$ does not converge to the unique minimizer $x_*$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:planar-degeneration}
0<\lambda_k\le C\|s_{k-1}\|\|s_k\|\longrightarrow0
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $k$, with $C$ independent of $k$.
Moreover, $\{H_k\}$ is bounded and $\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\to0$.

If $x_k$ does not converge to the unique minimizer $x_*$, then 0<\lambda_k\le C\|s_{k-1}\|\|s_k\|\longrightarrow0 for all sufficiently large $k$, with $C$ independent of $k$. Moreover, $\{H_k\}$ is bounded and $\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\to0$.

items.label: Theorem 13
items.statementLatex:
\label{thm:planar-convergence}
Let $f\in C^2(\R^2)$ satisfy $\nabla^2f(x)\succeq m I$ for all
$x\in\R^2$ and some $m>0$. Let $x_0\in\R^2$ and $H_0\succ0$
be arbitrary, and fix $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$. Suppose $\nabla^2f$ is locally
Lipschitz continuous on a neighborhood of the initial level set
$\mathcal L_0=\{x\in\R^2:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}$.
Then classical DFP with update \eqref{eq:dfp-update} and positive step
lengths satisfying \eqref{eq:armijo} and \eqref{eq:weak-curvature}
either reaches the unique minimizer $x_*$ in finitely many iterations or
generates an infinite sequence satisfying
$x_k\longrightarrow x_*$ and $\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\longrightarrow0$.

Suppose $ abla^2f$ is locally Lipschitz continuous on a neighborhood of the initial level set $\mathcal L_0=\{x\in\R^2:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}$. Then classical DFP with update [eq:dfp-update] and positive step lengths satisfying [eq:armijo] and [eq:weak-curvature] either reaches the unique minimizer $x_*$ in finitely many iterations or generates an infinite sequence satisfying $x_k\longrightarrow x_*$ and $\| abla f(x_k)\|\longrightarrow0$.
